types.name: FColorSpace
types.doc:
The IEC 61966-2-1 sRGB transfer pair, the same curve the GPU applies when
it samples or writes an _SRGB format. The plain pair does not clamp, so
values outside [0, 1] stay on the curve's linear and power segments; the
byte forms saturate first because a byte cannot hold anything else.

types.name: FColorVision
types.doc:
FColorVision — the colour-vision deficiency model the tonemap pass applies
(Tonemap.hlsl: ColorVisionMatrix, ApplyColorVisionSimulation,
ApplyColorVisionCorrection), on the CPU: Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes
2009 at severity 1, in linear light. Simulation shows what a viewer with
the deficiency sees; correction takes the difference that simulation lost
and folds it into the channels that viewer still separates. The shader and
this header carry the same numbers; the colour-vision row checks these.

members.signature: static void DecomposeMatrix(const Mat4& mat, Vec3& outPos, Vec3& outRot, Vec3& outScale)
members.doc:
Decompose a TRS matrix into position, rotation (euler radians), and scale.
Row-major layout: translation at m[0][3], m[1][3], m[2][3].
The euler comes out in the engine's Rx * Ry * Rz order so it feeds
straight back through Quat::FromEuler / TransformComponent::GetLocalMatrix
without changing the rotation.

members.name: FromEuler
members.doc:
Engine-wide euler convention: R = Rx(x) * Ry(y) * Rz(z), the same
order TransformComponent::GetLocalMatrix bakes into world matrices.
Any other composition here would make quat-driven rotations (actors,
physics, decomposed imports) disagree with what renders on screen.

members.name: ToEuler
members.doc:
Exact inverse of FromEuler (Rx * Ry * Rz decomposition). Component
mapping matches FRotator: x = Pitch (about X), y = Yaw (about the Y
up-axis), z = Roll (about Z). The asin-clamped axis is Y — triples
for |yaw| > 90 come back as an equivalent (x±π, mirrored y, z±π)
set, which recomposes to the identical rotation in this same order.

types.name: ECurveTangentMode
types.doc:
Who owns a key's tangents. Auto keys are re-derived from their neighbours
whenever the curve is edited; User keys keep what the artist dragged, with
both handles locked to one slope; Break lets arrive and leave differ.

types.name: ECurveExtrapolation
types.doc:
What a curve does before its first key and after its last (UE's
ERichCurveExtrapolation). Constant holds the end value, which is what every
curve written before extrapolation existed did, so it stays the default.

members.name: Linear
members.doc: continues along the end key's slope

members.name: Cycle
members.doc: repeats the keyed range

members.name: CycleWithOffset
members.doc: repeats it, each cycle shifted by the range's rise

members.name: Oscillate
members.doc: repeats it mirrored every other cycle

members.name: ArriveTangent
members.doc:
Tangents are slopes (dValue/dTime), UE-style: Leave on this key and
Arrive on the next shape the segment between them.

members.name: Keys
members.doc: kept sorted by Time

members.name: AddKey
members.signature: int32_t AddKey(float time, float value, ECurveInterp interp = ECurveInterp::Cubic)

members.name: AutoTangents
members.doc:
Catmull-Rom-style auto tangents: each Auto key's slope is the secant of
its neighbours (endpoint keys go flat) — the "just look smooth" default
every curve editor needs. User and Break keys are the artist's and are
left alone; ResetTangentsToAuto hands them back.

members.name: EdgeSlope
members.doc:
The slope a Linear extrapolation continues along: the end key's tangent
on a cubic end, the end segment's secant on a linear one, flat on a step.

members.name: Eval
members.signature: float Eval(float time, float defaultValue = 0.0f) const
members.doc:
Evaluate at `time`. Outside the key range the curve does what its
PreInfinity / PostInfinity say; Constant (the default) clamps to the end
value, because extrapolation surprises are worse than flat ends for
tuning data that never asked for them.
